To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the direction and the magnitude of the immune response to DNA vaccination against HSP65 could be modulated by co-injecting a TH1 or TH2 cytokine gene as an adjuvant.
the direction and the magnitude of immune response to DNA vaccination against mycobacterial heat shock protein 63 could be modulated by co-injection with cytokine genes as an adjuvant.
cytokines can be used to modulate immune response generated by DNA vaccine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cytokines in DNA-based vaccine against M. tuberculosis.
developing a new strategy for DNA vaccine adjuvants.
the development of a new strategy for DNA-based vaccines by using cytokine gene as an adjuvant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cytokines play different roles in different stages of immune response and that the effects of a particular cytokine gene as an adjuvant depend on the nature of antigen, route and timing of immunization, and other immunological factors.
the immune response in DNA immunization can be modulated and directed in a desired way by co-administration of an appropriate cytokines as adjuvant.
the cytokine adjuvant should be selected on a case by case basis, depending on the nature of the antigen and the desired immune response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNA vaccines could be designed to elicit a specific immune response by co-injecting a cytokine gene as an adjuvant.
the cytokine gene adjoivants could be used to enhance specific immune response in a manner that is dependent upon the nature and the magnitude of the immune response that is to be achieved.
the cytokines IL-12, GM-CSF, IL-18, Eta-1 and Flt3L are all effective in enhancing cellular immunity to DNA vaccination against M. tuberculosis Hsp65.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytokine adjuvant can be used to enhance the protective immunity against M. tuberculosis by DNA vaccination.
DNA vaccines are highly flexible and can be manipulated to induce different types of immune responses.
the choice of adjuvant is crucial for the development of an effective DNA vaccine.
